newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nail shares leap on Johnnic deal.
newsitem.headline: Nail shares leap on Johnnic deal.

text.p: New Africa Investments Ltd shares leapt on Thursday on news of the sale of Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd's of most of its 47.4 stake in Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd (Johnnic) to a black interest group.

Nail, an industrial holding company with interests in the media sector, is part of the 50-member National Empowerment Consortium (NEC) which has concluded the deal with Anglo to buy Johnnic, valued at 4.2 billion rand, at a discount to its market price.
"It is on the back of the Johnnic deal. If you are buying an asset at a discount and have an option to buy more at a further discount, it has to be good for Nail," a dealer said.
The share initially leapt to an intraday high of 290 cents -- up 16 percent from its previous 250 cents close, but had retraced to 274 by early afternoon on profit-taking.
Trade was described as brisk although volumes were moderate, with about 100,000 shares changing hands valued at about 283,000 rand.

In terms of the deal, the NEC will purchase an initial shareholding of at least 20 percent in Johnnic at 50 rand per share -- against a current price of 56 rand -- and will have an 18-month option to take its stake to 35 percent.
A further six percent will be made available via a retail offering by the NEC to smaller NEC members and others within the black community.
Johnnic's assets include substantial stakes in leading concerns such as South African Breweries, Toyota South Africa, Premier Group and Times Media .
Dealers said Nail was well focussed and its interests in Times Media Ltd, a healthy media company which has posted consistent profits, would boost its earnings.
"Nail is well focussed and well managed. It has indicated that it is really targeting Times Media which has shown profits in past years."
Dealers said Nail's publication, New Nation, had been making losses and denting Nail's earnings.
"Nail has been struggling with New Nation. It seems something will be done to New Nation, it might be closed down and this will plug a hole in their profits," one said.
Benefits from Johnnic were seen coming through in the next three years.
"The Johnnic deal will take a while. It is not going to reflect on their results now but in the next two to three years. (But) Nail is certainly a good share," one said.
At 1140 GMT, Anglo was trading 150 cents higher at 269,50 rand, while Johnnic was 25 cents lower at 55.75 rand.
